mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and damage GI mucosa; warfarin inhibits clotting factors
effect: Greatly increased risk of GI bleeding and haemorrhage
management: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for analgesia. If NSAID essential, add PPI and monitor INR closely.

mechanism: Dual antiplatelet and anticoagulant effect; aspirin damages GI mucosa
effect: Increased bleeding risk, especially GI
management: Only combine if clear indication (e.g. mechanical valve). Add PPI. Monitor INR.

mechanism: Antibiotics alter gut flora reducing vitamin K synthesis; some inhibit warfarin metabolism
effect: INR may rise, increasing bleeding risk
management: Monitor INR more frequently during antibiotic course. Adjust warfarin dose as needed.

mechanism: Fluconazole is a potent CYP2C9 inhibitor, blocking warfarin metabolism
effect: Markedly elevated INR and high bleeding risk
management: Reduce warfarin dose by 25-50%. Monitor INR at days 3-5. Consider alternative antifungal.

mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, reducing warfarin clearance
effect: Elevated INR and increased bleeding risk
management: Reduce warfarin dose. Monitor INR closely during and after treatment.

mechanism: Both reduce potassium excretion; ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone
effect: Hyperkalaemia, potentially causing cardiac arrhythmia
management: Monitor potassium within 1 week. Avoid in renal impairment. Use lowest doses.

mechanism: Both cause potassium retention through different mechanisms
effect: Risk of life-threatening hyperkalaemia
management: Monitor potassium and renal function. Start spironolactone at low dose. Avoid if eGFR <30.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins, opposing ACE inhibitor vasodilation
effect: Reduced antihypertensive effect, increased risk of AKI and hyperkalaemia
management: Avoid prolonged NSAID use. Monitor renal function and blood pressure.

mechanism: Combined serotonergic activity overwhelms serotonin metabolism
effect: Serotonin syndrome: hyperthermia, rigidity, myoclonus, autonomic instability, potentially fatal
management: Absolutely contraindicated. Minimum 2-week washout between SSRI and MAOI (5 weeks for fluoxetine).

mechanism: Tramadol has serotonin reuptake inhibition activity; additive serotonergic effect
effect: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures
management: Use with caution. Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms. Consider alternative analgesic.

mechanism: SSRIs deplete platelet serotonin; NSAIDs inhibit COX and damage GI mucosa
effect: Increased GI bleeding risk (3-6 fold)
management: Add gastroprotection (PPI) if combination necessary. Consider paracetamol instead.

mechanism: SSRIs inhibit CYP2C9 (fluoxetine, fluvoxamine) and deplete platelet serotonin
effect: Increased INR and bleeding risk
management: Monitor INR closely when starting/stopping SSRI. Choose sertraline/citalopram (less interaction).

mechanism: Clarithromycin/erythromycin inhibit CYP3A4, blocking statin metabolism
effect: Rhabdomyolysis risk due to elevated statin levels
management: Pause statin during short macrolide course, or use azithromycin (no CYP3A4 inhibition).

mechanism: Grapefruit inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, increasing statin bioavailability
effect: Increased statin levels and myopathy risk (simvastatin, atorvastatin)
management: Avoid grapefruit with simvastatin. Small amounts acceptable with atorvastatin. Rosuvastatin unaffected.

mechanism: Both cause myotoxicity through different mechanisms; gemfibrozil inhibits statin glucuronidation
effect: Significantly increased rhabdomyolysis risk
management: Avoid gemfibrozil + statin. If fibrate needed, use fenofibrate. Monitor CK and symptoms.

mechanism: Contrast may cause AKI; metformin accumulates in renal failure
effect: Risk of lactic acidosis
management: Withhold metformin on day of contrast and 48h after. Check renal function before restarting.

mechanism: Both inhibit gluconeogenesis and alcohol impairs lactate metabolism
effect: Increased risk of lactic acidosis and hypoglycaemia
management: Limit alcohol intake. Avoid binge drinking. Monitor blood glucose.

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and renal clearance of digoxin
effect: Digoxin toxicity (nausea, arrhythmia, visual disturbance)
management: Halve digoxin dose when starting amiodarone. Monitor digoxin levels at 1 week.

mechanism: Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein and renal tubular secretion of digoxin
effect: Elevated digoxin levels; additive AV nodal depression
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 25-50%. Monitor levels and ECG. Avoid in heart block.

mechanism: Thiazides cause hypokalaemia, which sensitises the heart to digoxin
effect: Digoxin toxicity even at therapeutic levels
management: Monitor potassium regularly. Supplement potassium or add potassium-sparing diuretic.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins, decreasing lithium clearance
effect: Lithium toxicity (tremor, confusion, renal damage, seizures)
management: Avoid NSAIDs or monitor lithium levels closely. Use paracetamol for analgesia.

mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce GFR and sodium reabsorption, decreasing lithium excretion
effect: Lithium toxicity
management: Monitor lithium levels when starting ACE inhibitor. Reduce lithium dose if needed.

mechanism: Thiazides increase proximal tubular reabsorption of lithium
effect: Lithium toxicity
management: Avoid combination. If necessary, reduce lithium dose and monitor levels weekly.

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to active metabolite
effect: Reduced antiplatelet efficacy, increased cardiovascular risk
management: Use pantoprazole or lansoprazole instead (less CYP2C19 inhibition).

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, blocking theophylline metabolism
effect: Theophylline toxicity (seizures, arrhythmia, nausea)
management: Reduce theophylline dose by 30-50%. Monitor theophylline levels. Consider alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin is a potent CYP1A2 inhibitor; tizanidine is solely CYP1A2 metabolised
effect: 10-fold increase in tizanidine levels; severe hypotension, sedation
management: Combination is contraindicated. Use alternative antibiotic or muscle relaxant.

mechanism: Both are folate antagonists; trimethoprim reduces renal clearance of methotrexate
effect: Pancytopenia and methotrexate toxicity
management: Avoid combination. If co-trimoxazole essential, monitor FBC closely. Ensure adequate folate supplementation.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate
effect: Methotrexate toxicity (mucositis, pancytopenia, hepatotoxicity)
management: Avoid NSAIDs with high-dose methotrexate. Low-dose: use with caution, monitor FBC and renal function.

mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, blocking carbamazepine metabolism
effect: Carbamazepine toxicity (ataxia, diplopia, nystagmus, drowsiness)
management: Avoid combination. Use azithromycin (no CYP3A4 inhibition) or alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, increasing metabolism of ethinylestradiol
effect: Contraceptive failure
management: Use non-hormonal or high-dose methods. Consider depot medroxyprogesterone or copper IUD.

mechanism: Both depress AV conduction and myocardial contractility
effect: Severe bradycardia, heart block, heart failure, asystole
management: IV combination is contraindicated. Oral combination only with extreme caution under specialist supervision.

mechanism: Beta-blockers mask hypoglycaemia symptoms (tremor, tachycardia) and impair glycogenolysis
effect: Unrecognised and prolonged hypoglycaemia
management: Use cardioselective beta-blocker (bisoprolol). Educate patient on alternative hypo signs (sweating persists).

mechanism: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin levels
effect: Increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
management: Limit simvastatin to 20mg daily with amlodipine. Consider switching to atorvastatin or rosuvastatin.

mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, retaining potassium
effect: Hyperkalaemia
management: Avoid routine potassium supplementation with ACE inhibitors. Monitor potassium levels.

mechanism: Both release nitric oxide, causing vasodilation
effect: Profound and potentially fatal hypotension
management: Combination is absolutely contraindicated. Do not give nitrate within 24h of sildenafil (48h for tadalafil).

mechanism: Both prolong QT interval through different cardiac ion channel effects
effect: Risk of Torsades de Pointes and sudden cardiac death
management: Avoid combination. ECG monitoring if unavoidable. Choose alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: Fluoxetine potently inhibits CYP2D6, blocking conversion of tamoxifen to active endoxifen
effect: Reduced tamoxifen efficacy, potentially increased breast cancer recurrence
management: Use SSRI with minimal CYP2D6 inhibition (sertraline, citalopram, escitalopram, venlafaxine).

mechanism: Complex: valproate displaces phenytoin from protein binding and inhibits its metabolism
effect: Phenytoin toxicity despite normal total levels (free fraction increased)
management: Monitor free phenytoin levels. Adjust doses carefully. Monitor for toxicity signs.

mechanism: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking azathioprine metabolism via 6-mercaptopurine
effect: Severe myelosuppression (pancytopenia, potentially fatal)
management: Reduce azathioprine dose by 75% if allopurinol essential. Monitor FBC weekly initially.

mechanism: Both prolong QT interval
effect: Risk of ventricular arrhythmia and Torsades de Pointes
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative anti-emetic (metoclopramide with caution, or ondansetron).

mechanism: Trimethoprim acts like amiloride in the distal nephron, retaining potassium
effect: Hyperkalaemia, especially in elderly and renal impairment
management: Monitor potassium within 1 week of starting. Avoid in eGFR <30. Short courses preferred.

mechanism: Thiazide increases lithium reabsorption in proximal tubule
effect: Lithium toxicity
management: Avoid if possible. If essential, monitor lithium levels frequently. Consider loop diuretic instead.

mechanism: Both lower seizure threshold and have serotonergic activity
effect: Increased seizure risk and serotonin syndrome risk
management: Avoid combination if possible. If used, monitor for seizures and serotonin syndrome symptoms.

mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, blocking colchicine clearance
effect: Colchicine toxicity (potentially fatal multi-organ failure)
management: Contraindicated in renal/hepatic impairment. If used, reduce colchicine dose significantly.

mechanism: Ketoconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, both of which clear rivaroxaban
effect: Markedly increased rivaroxaban levels and bleeding risk
management: Combination is contraindicated. Use alternative antifungal (fluconazole has less effect).

mechanism: Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein, increasing dabigatran absorption
effect: Increased dabigatran levels and bleeding risk
management: Reduce dabigatran dose. Take dabigatran 2 hours before verapamil. Monitor for bleeding.

mechanism: Additive glucose-lowering effect; thiazolidinediones cause fluid retention
effect: Hypoglycaemia and increased heart failure risk
management: Reduce insulin dose when adding TZD. Monitor for oedema and heart failure symptoms.

mechanism: Diclofenac may interfere with aspirin binding to COX-1 platelets
effect: Reduced cardioprotective effect of low-dose aspirin; increased GI bleeding
management: Take aspirin 2 hours before diclofenac. Add PPI. Prefer ibuprofen alternative if possible.

mechanism: Both are ototoxic; furosemide increases gentamicin concentration in inner ear
effect: Irreversible ototoxicity and increased nephrotoxicity
management: Avoid combination if possible. Monitor gentamicin levels and renal function closely.

mechanism: Both damage GI mucosa through different mechanisms
effect: Significantly increased risk of peptic ulcer and GI bleeding
management: Add PPI if combination necessary. Monitor for GI symptoms. Shortest course possible.

mechanism: Divalent cations (Ca, Mg, Al) chelate doxycycline, preventing absorption
effect: Reduced doxycycline efficacy
management: Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Same applies to iron and dairy products.

mechanism: Both independently increase tendon damage risk
effect: Increased risk of tendon rupture (especially Achilles)
management: Avoid combination in patients >60, renal impairment, or on chronic corticosteroids. Stop if tendon pain develops.

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin levels
effect: Increased rhabdomyolysis risk
management: Limit simvastatin to 20mg daily. Consider switching to fluvastatin or pravastatin (less affected).

mechanism: Spironolactone retains potassium; supplementation adds more
effect: Dangerous hyperkalaemia
management: Avoid potassium supplements with spironolactone. Monitor potassium levels regularly.

mechanism: Fluvoxamine is a potent CYP1A2 inhibitor; theophylline is CYP1A2 metabolised
effect: Theophylline toxicity (nausea, arrhythmia, seizures)
management: Combination contraindicated. Use alternative SSRI (sertraline, citalopram).

mechanism: Metoclopramide blocks dopamine receptors, opposing levodopa effect
effect: Worsening Parkinsonian symptoms; reduced levodopa efficacy
management: Avoid combination. Use domperidone as anti-emetic (does not cross blood-brain barrier effectively).

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, the major metabolic pathway for clozapine
effect: Elevated clozapine levels causing seizures, sedation, neutropenia
management: Reduce clozapine dose by 50% if ciprofloxacin necessary. Monitor clozapine levels. Use alternative antibiotic.

mechanism: Macrolides inhibit CYP3A4, blocking ergotamine metabolism
effect: Ergotism: severe peripheral vasospasm, gangrene
management: Combination is contraindicated. Use triptans for migraine if antibiotic needed.

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, the main metabolic pathway for glipizide/glibenclamide
effect: Prolonged hypoglycaemia
management: Monitor blood glucose closely. Consider reducing sulfonylurea dose during fluconazole course.
